statements.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the most transformational technology in the history of the world — and will have a profound impact on the life of every man, woman and child in our country. And, if you’re currently in the workforce, there’s a good chance it will take your job.
statements.venue: Op-ed (Fox News), posted on Sanders' Senate site

statements.text: The reality is that the AI oligarchs do not want to just replace specific jobs. They want to replace workers.
statements.venue: Op-ed (Fox News), posted on Sanders' Senate site

statements.text: Why would any business want to hire a human worker when it can install AI and robotics and cut its labor costs by 80 to 90%? AI and robots don’t take a salary, need a vacation, require health care, or form a union. They just keep working — 24/7.
statements.venue: Op-ed (Fox News), posted on Sanders' Senate site

statements.text: As the ranking member of the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee (HELP Committee), I released a report today finding that AI, automation and robotics could replace nearly 100 million jobs in America over the next decade, including 40% of registered nurses, 47% of truck drivers, 64% of accountants, 65% of teaching assistants and 89% of fast food workers, among many other occupations. And as bad as that may seem, I am afraid it may be an underestimate.
statements.venue: Op-ed on Sanders' Senate site

statements.text: First, we must move to a 32-hour workweek with no loss in pay. Think about it: today, American workers are 400% more productive than they were in the 1940s, when the 40-hour workweek was first established. Artificial intelligence and robotics will greatly accelerate that productivity.
statements.venue: Op-ed on Sanders' Senate site

statements.text: Congress must act. That is why I have introduced legislation, with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, to impose a federal moratorium on the construction of new AI data centers until strong national safeguards are in place.
statements.venue: Op-ed (Wall Street Journal), posted on Sanders' Senate site

statements.text: “When scientists tell you there is a chance, a chance that it could have a cataclysmic impact on humanity, you’ve got to be a moron not to say, ‘Slow it down.’”
statements.venue: BBC Newsnight interview

statements.text: “And if it wipes out humanity, what are you going to do with all those billions and trillions of dollars?”
statements.venue: BBC Newsnight interview

[...] This is precisely why the Constitution of the United States and U.S. law make it illegal for Presidents to accept gifts from foreign powers.
statements.context: Senate floor speech during a motion to discharge joint resolutions of disapproval blocking arms sales to the UAE and Qatar.

statements.text: That is why I have called for a moratorium on new AI data centers until we make sure that the economic gains of these revolutionary technologies benefit the working families of this country and not just a handful of multibillionaires in Silicon Valley.
statements.context: Senator Bernie Sanders speaks on the Senate floor during debate on the Motion to Proceed to the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026.

statements.text: Further, and frighteningly, some very knowledgeable people fear that what was once seen as science fiction could soon become a reality, and that is that superintelligent AI could become smarter than humans, could become independent of human control, and pose an existential threat to the human race. [...] Let me also say that I am deeply concerned about the existential threat posed by AI.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Sen. Bernie Sanders on AI and robotics, announcing planned legislation for a moratorium on new AI data centers.

statements.text: And it is not only what it will do to throwing millions of workers off of their jobs, hooking children to artificial intelligence. I have talked to a number of scientists who believe that we are not talking about science fiction anymore in the sense that if AI continues to develop and become smarter than humans, the truth is AI may become independent of human control and threaten the very existence of humanity.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator Bernie Sanders during debate on the SAFEGUARD American Voter Eligibility Act, pivoting from social spending to AI risks.

statements.text: “AI and robotics are creating the most sweeping technological revolution in the history of humanity. The scale, scope and speed of that change is unprecedented. Congress is way behind where it should be in understanding the nature of this revolution and its impacts,” Sanders said. “Bottom line: We cannot sit back and allow a handful of billionaire Big Tech oligarchs to make decisions that will reshape our economy, our democracy and the future of humanity. We need serious public debate and democratic oversight over this enormously consequential issue. The time for action is now. We need a federal moratorium on AI data centers.”
statements.venue: Press release on AI Data Center Moratorium Act

statements.text: “Despite the extraordinary importance of this issue and its impact on every man, woman and child in this country, AI has received far too little serious discussion here in our nation’s capital,” Sanders told reporters on Wednesday. “I fear that Congress is totally unprepared for the magnitude of the changes that are already taking place.”
statements.venue: News conference remarks, reported by The Guardian

statements.text: “A moratorium will give us time — time to understand the risks, time to protect working families, time to defend our democracy and time to ensure that this technology works for all of us, not just the few,”
statements.venue: News conference, reported by The Hill

statements.text: “They understand that these billionaires are investing huge amounts of money into AI and robotics, not to improve life for working families, but to dramatically increase their own wealth and power,” Sanders said. “You think the average American is sitting around trusting that the multibillionaires are going to transform society for the good of ordinary people? I don’t think so.”
statements.venue: News conference, reported by Roll Call

statements.text: When I convened leading American and Chinese scientists at the U.S. Capitol, they warned that the world is woefully unprepared for the threats posed by the rapid and uncontrolled development of artificial intelligence. That is why I welcome the news that the U.S. and China are planning to discuss the risks related to AI this week. Trump and Xi must seize this moment to make clear that humans, not machines, come first.
statements.venue: Press release: statement on U.S.-China AI talks

statements.text: At the height of the Cold War, Reagan and Gorbachev found a way to negotiate nuclear arms control. The existential risk posed by AI demands nothing less from Trump and Xi.
statements.venue: Press release: statement on U.S.-China AI talks

statements.text: Further, there is a very real fear that as AI becomes smarter than humans, it could eventually function independent of human control with potentially catastrophic consequences. [...] That is why in the coming weeks, I will be introducing the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator Bernie Sanders introducing the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, proposing public ownership stakes in major AI companies.

statements.text: Now, I would say, lastly, Bob, I, as you may know, have met with Nobel Prize-winning scientists, and what they are saying to me is, Bernie, it is not a question of whether AI will become smarter than humans. It will sooner or later. And when that happens, there is a possibility, Bob, that it may become independent of human control.
statements.venue: Vermont Public interview

statements.text: And yet, as disturbing as all of this is, there is another even more alarming danger posed by AI. And that is that, if AI surpasses human intelligence as many scientists believe could happen, this technology will escape human control with potentially catastrophic consequences.
statements.venue: Prepared remarks at Pro-Human Assembly

statements.text: Scientists have been clear: AI is an existential threat to humanity. Congress and governments around the world must act now before it is too late.
statements.venue: Prepared remarks at Pro-Human Assembly

statements.text: Like nuclear weapons, artificial superintelligence is a threat to humanity — and it must be treated as such.
statements.venue: Prepared remarks at Pro-Human Assembly

statements.text: And that is why I have introduced legislation — the AI American Sovereign Wealth Fund Act — that would require that half of the board members of AI companies be appointed by the public. The Big Tech oligarchs must no longer be allowed to determine the future of humanity.
statements.venue: Prepared remarks at Pro-Human Assembly

statements.text: And let’s be clear: A superintelligent AI that escapes human control will not be an American problem. It will not be a Chinese problem. It will be humanity’s problem.
statements.venue: Prepared remarks at Pro-Human Assembly
